problem_text:
A logistics manager is preparing a shipment for a transcontinental freight run. They must select a collection of cargo containers to maximize total revenue while adhering to the aircraft's payload limit.

The available containers are:
* Container 1: mass 42kg, revenue 285 credits
* Container 2: mass 12kg, revenue 288 credits
* Container 3: mass 26kg, revenue 126 credits
* Container 4: mass 16kg, revenue 272 credits
* Container 5: mass 6kg, revenue 21 credits
* Container 6: mass 49kg, revenue 197 credits
* Container 7: mass 1kg, revenue 102 credits
* Container 8: mass 20kg, revenue 215 credits
* Container 9: mass 31kg, revenue 40 credits
* Container 10: mass 10kg, revenue 196 credits
* Container 11: mass 49kg, revenue 73 credits
* Container 12: mass 20kg, revenue 84 credits
* Container 13: mass 25kg, revenue 225 credits
* Container 14: mass 43kg, revenue 259 credits
* Container 15: mass 31kg, revenue 175 credits
* Container 16: mass 47kg, revenue 300 credits
* Container 17: mass 11kg, revenue 137 credits
* Container 18: mass 23kg, revenue 172 credits
* Container 19: mass 40kg, revenue 97 credits
* Container 20: mass 37kg, revenue 218 credits
* Container 21: mass 48kg, revenue 205 credits
* Container 22: mass 22kg, revenue 177 credits
* Container 23: mass 48kg, revenue 287 credits
* Container 24: mass 27kg, revenue 83 credits
* Container 25: mass 29kg, revenue 50 credits
* Container 26: mass 42kg, revenue 165 credits
* Container 27: mass 25kg, revenue 110 credits
* Container 28: mass 2kg, revenue 277 credits
* Container 29: mass 50kg, revenue 234 credits
* Container 30: mass 15kg, revenue 166 credits

Furthermore, due to a contractual exclusivity clause, exactly one of Container 1 and Container 2 must be included in the shipment.

If Container 3 is included, it necessitates special handling equipment that reduces the effective payload capacity of the aircraft by 10 kg.
The aircraft's maximum permissible payload is 592 kg. The manager must determine which containers to load.
